function.name: get_weather_forecast
function.description: Retrieves the weather forecast for a specified location and date range. The forecast includes temperature, precipitation, and wind speed. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which the weather forecast is requested, in the format of 'City, Country' (e.g., 'London, UK').

start_date.description: The start date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-01').

end_date.description: The end date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-07').

units.description: The unit system in which to return the weather forecast data.

include_details.description: Specifies whether to include detailed forecast information such as humidity and visibility.

### How Turbonomics Helps Unilever Leverage AI for Multi‑Cloud Observability | Goal | What Turbonomics Provides | Why It Matters for Unilever | |------|---------------------------|-----------------------------| | **Unified Visibility Across All Clouds** | • **Single pane of glass** that aggregates metrics from GCP, AWS, Azure, on‑prem, and edge environments.
• Real‑time dashboards with AI‑driven anomaly detection. | Unilever can see the health of its global supply‑chain, retail, and consumer‑engagement workloads in one place, reducing blind spots that siloed native tools create. | | **Predictive Capacity Planning** | • Uses machine‑learning models to forecast CPU, memory, I/O, and network usage 24–48 h ahead.
• Suggests right‑size resources before performance degrades. | Enables Unilever to avoid over‑provisioning (cost) or under‑provisioning (service outages) across its multi‑cloud portfolio. | | **Automated Remediation & Optimization** | • AI‑based policy engine that automatically moves workloads, throttles traffic, or scales resources based on business priorities.
• Integrates with Kubernetes, OpenShift, and legacy VMs. | Reduces manual toil for Unilever’s ops teams and ensures that critical consumer‑facing services always meet SLAs. | | **Cost Transparency & Forecasting** | • Consolidated cost view across all clouds, with AI‑driven cost‑saving recommendations.
• Predictive budgeting and chargeback/showback capabilities. | Gives Unilever finance a clear picture of where money is spent and where savings can be realized, supporting strategic investment decisions. | | **Compliance & Governance** | • Policy‑based controls that enforce data residency, security, and regulatory requirements across clouds.
• Automated audit trails and reporting. | Helps Unilever maintain compliance with GDPR, CCPA, and other regional regulations while operating globally. | #### How It Works in Practice 1. **Data Collection** – Turbonomics pulls telemetry (CPU, memory, network, logs, etc.) from each cloud provider via APIs, agents, or native monitoring services. 2. **AI Engine** – A central ML model ingests this telemetry, learns normal patterns, and flags anomalies or inefficiencies. 3. **Decision Layer** – Based on business‑defined policies (e.g., “Retail website must stay below 95 % CPU”), the system recommends or automatically applies changes (scale‑up, scale‑down, migrate). 4. **Feedback Loop** – Outcomes of actions feed back into the model, improving accuracy over time. --- ### Difference Between Turbonomics and Native Cloud Monitoring Tools | Feature | Turbonomics | Native Cloud Tools (GCP, AWS, Azure) | |---------|-------------|-------------------------------------| | **Scope** | Cross‑cloud + on‑prem + edge | Single‑cloud only | | **Unified Dashboard** | One UI for all clouds | Separate dashboards per provider | | **AI‑Driven Insights** | Predictive analytics, anomaly detection, automated remediation | Mostly reactive alerts; limited predictive capability | | **Cost Optimization** | Consolidated cost view + AI recommendations | Cost Explorer/Cost Management per cloud; no cross‑cloud consolidation | | **Policy‑Based Automation** | Central policy engine that spans clouds | Policies are provider‑specific;
